clue.text: If you don't speculate'

parts.note: the clue is the first half of a proverb about risk

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'nothing venture, nothing gain': the clue paraphrases the condition, and the answer is its opening words.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means that without a risky outlay there is no reward, so declining to speculate is this phrase's case.

clue.text: Inspiring a come-back ?

parts.note: not a sporting revival but a longing for the past, a wish for old times to come back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come-back' suggests a sports or showbiz revival; it means the wish for bygone days to return.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful longing for the past makes one want earlier days restored, the feeling of homesickness for former times.

clue.text: " Where subjects' feet May hourly on their sovereign's head (Richard II)

definitions.text: " Where subjects' feet May hourly on their sovereign's head (Richard II)

parts.words: " Where subjects' feet May hourly on their sovereign's head (Richard II)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation: the missing verb comes from King Richard's speech imagining burial in the king's highway

explanation.walkthrough: In Richard II, the king imagines being buried in the highway, 'where subjects' feet may hourly trample on their sovereign's head'. The page marks the gap with a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: The deposed king pictures passers-by treading heavily over his grave, the crushing walk of the missing verb.

clue.text: Clueless is he? We wouldn't know !'

definitions.meaning: an ignorant person, one with no clue
the Latin word means 'we do not know', once written by grand juries on bills they rejected

explanation.definitionFit: The English word for a know-nothing comes from Latin legal usage meaning 'we are ignorant (of it)'.

clue.text: Startled reaction to some Degas paintings

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Gallery visitors are taken aback by certain works of the French Impressionist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp intake of breath is the typical shocked response to a surprise.

clue.text: See 1
In France it portrays all about one in poetry

definitions.note: the palace and town near Paris are a place in France

indicators.note: the pair of letters plus extras goes inside the word for poetry

parts.note: verses are lines of poetry

indicators.note: the word all wraps around the letter for one

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A French work depicts everything about a single person in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps ALL round I to make AILL, which 'in' places inside the poetry word. 'it portrays' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal palace of Louis XIV stands in a town just outside Paris, a famous French location.

clue.text: Ingenuous one in the body of the kirk

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the word for the main part of a church

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church; kirk is the Scottish word for church
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A trusting soul sits in the middle of a Scottish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I (one) inside NAVE, the central part of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ingenuous is innocent and unworldly, a synonym for credulous simplicity.

clue.text: Disentangle the new unit

annotationWithheld.why: Disentangle the new unit (7): UNTWINE is an anagram of NEW UNIT, but the only anagram signal is 'Disentangle', which is also the definition, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: It's due to come off in the seventies

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the clue word that follows, between its outer letters

explanation.surface: Something scheduled to take place at some point during the 1970s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come off' means take place, as an occasion does; the letters sit in 'seventies'.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion that is scheduled to happen is something expected to take place, a happening.

clue.text: A watering-place in plain locality here ?

definitions.note: the song line 'the rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain' puts a plain in this country

parts.note: a spa is a resort town with mineral springs, a watering-place
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether a spa resort can be found out on some flat plain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the line from My Fair Lady, 'the rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous elocution line locates that plain in the Iberian kingdom, so the country is where the plain is.

clue.text: It makes a non-U appearance in the ring on board

definitions.text: It makes a non-U appearance in the ring on board

parts.words: It makes a non-U appearance in the ring on board
parts.note: a table napkin appears rolled in a napkin ring on the dining table (the board), and its French-derived name was famously judged non-U, lower-middle-class usage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' and 'board' suggest boxing or a ship, but the ring is a napkin ring and the board is a dining table. 'Non-U' was 1950s British slang for words the upper class avoided.
explanation.definitionFit: This word for a table napkin was branded non-U, the class marker of speech the upper classes shunned.

clue.text: Be ambitious for praise

parts.note: to long for high achievement and the acclaim it brings

explanation.walkthrough: As a bonus, the letters of PRAISE can be rearranged into the answer, though no word in the clue signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: To hope and strive for something lofty, such as glory or recognition, is to have ambition directed at it.

clue.text: Rejuvenation of the front elevation

parts.note: the face of a building is its front
a lift is a raising, an elevation

explanation.surface: An architect describes giving a building's front a fresh look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front elevation' reads as one architect's term for a drawing of a façade; split it into two words, each giving its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery that tightens the skin is done to restore a youthful look, a kind of rejuvenation.

clue.text: Feelings of guilt ? Jack has the answer !

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to what remedies guilt rather than a synonym for it

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword sailor
a solution is an answer

explanation.surface: A sufferer of guilty conscience is told that a man named Jack can solve it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works with the question mark: forgiveness is the answer to feelings of guilt, the remedy, not the feelings themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgiveness of sins pronounced by a priest relieves the penitent's conscience, the cure for guilt.

clue.text: "Whither is fed the visionary ?" (Wordsworth)

parts.note: a fill-in quotation: the missing word ends a famous line in Wordsworth's Intimations of Immortality ode

explanation.walkthrough: The line is 'Whither is fled the visionary gleam?' from Wordsworth's Immortality Ode; the OCR dropped the L of 'fled' and the dash marking the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's line mourns the lost radiance of childhood vision, the faint shining light he names in the missing word.

clue.text: A good look-out for Apollo

parts.note: a raised turret built for the view is a fine look-out, and the famous Vatican statue of Apollo takes its name from such a turret

explanation.walkthrough: The Apollo Belvedere is a classical marble statue named after the Vatican's Belvedere courtyard, and the word itself means a raised summerhouse built for its view.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian word for a viewing tower ('fine view'), and the name given to the celebrated statue of the sun god.

clue.text: No change for him in a nudist camp ?

definitions.text: No change for him in a nudist camp ?

parts.words: No change for him in a nudist camp ?
parts.note: the biblical line asking whether this man can change his skin: among nudists, skin is all anyone wears, so he has nothing to change

explanation.walkthrough: Jeremiah 13:23 asks 'Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?'. 'Change' also means changing clothes, which nudists never do.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture names a man of the African nation whose skin cannot be altered, so 'no change' fits him.

clue.text: A necessity under cane punishment

indicators.note: the letters are given rough treatment, beaten into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's view that a beating with the cane must simply be borne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punishment' rearranges UNDER CANE. The surface makes the definition apt: stamina is needed by a pupil being caned.
explanation.definitionFit: The capacity to bear hardship without giving way is required when suffering a caning.

clue.text: Contends successfully with sound quality in building

definitions.note: a stone used in building, laid as the top course of a wall

parts.note: to cope with something is to deal with it successfully
tone is the character or quality of a sound

explanation.surface: Praise for a builder who manages both acoustics and construction well.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a coping stone, a part found in building, placed at the top of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A coping stone caps a wall in masonry construction, so it is a component used in building work.

clue.text: Father can get a rise, he has swagger

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that rises is read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad can expect a pay rise and struts about with confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get a rise' turns CAN to NAC, read upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant confidence and dash of manner is a synonym for a swaggering style.

clue.text: What the woodman did when taking a wife?

parts.note: split as two words, the answer says a man married: the pronoun for him plus the verb for marrying

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a forester did on his wedding day.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'he wed', the answer describes a man taking a wife; read whole, it is what a woodman does to timber with an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodman chops trees, and the past tense of chopping with an axe is this verb.

clue.text: Malevolently stingy ?

parts.note: not mean with money but quick to sting, like a spiteful insect

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stingy' suggests miserly, but here it means given to stinging, as a yellow-and-black insect is.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable and spiteful in manner, like the stinging insect the word is formed from.

clue.text: Where spirits are confined in Tartarean torment

definitions.meaning: a locking stand for decanters of whisky or brandy, which keeps the liquor visible but out of reach
the mythical king punished in Tartarus by water and fruit forever just out of his reach

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' suggests ghosts in the underworld, matching the second half, but it means liquor kept in a locked decanter stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The decanter stand is named after the Greek king whose punishment in the underworld was to see food and drink he could never take.

clue.text: Lock, centre-half, gets a couple of bob

indicators.note: half of the word centre is taken, its second three letters

parts.note: bob is old British slang for a shilling, abbreviated s, so two of them give two letters s

explanation.surface: A footballer playing centre-half gets two shillings for a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre-half' looks like a football position but means the second half of the word 'centre'. A bob was a shilling in pre-decimal British money, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock of hair is a curl or strand, the same as a ringlet of hair.

clue.text: Monarch twice beheaded in France

definitions.note: a town in Provence, so a place in France

indicators.note: the king's name loses its first letter, then its new first letter, two heads cut off in turn

parts.note: Charles is the name of many kings

explanation.surface: A king loses his head two times over somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice beheaded' takes off C and then H from CHARLES. Arles is a town in Provence painted by Van Gogh.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman city on the Rhône in southern France, a French town.

clue.text: His return puts an end to the play

definitions.text: His return puts an end to the play

parts.words: His return puts an end to the play
parts.note: the saying 'when the cat's away the mice will play': once the hunting cat comes back, the playing stops

explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' tempts a solver to write a word backwards and 'play' suggests theatre, but this is the proverb of the mice playing while the cat is away.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat kept to catch rodents is the hunter whose absence lets the mice play, so his coming back ends it.

clue.text: An unwelcome catch-for astronauts?

parts.note: a crustacean that nips a fisherman is a catch no one wants, and astronomers know a nebula of the same name in Taurus

explanation.walkthrough: To 'catch a crab' is a rowing blunder, an unwanted catch; the Crab Nebula is the space connection the astronauts hint at.
explanation.definitionFit: The sideways-walking shellfish names a rowing mishap and a famous nebula, linking both halves.

clue.text: Alpine climbing device

parts.note: the Latin motto ('ever higher') on the banner of the youth climbing through an Alpine village in Longfellow's poem

explanation.walkthrough: 'Device' means a heraldic motto, not a gadget: Longfellow's poem has a youth carrying a banner with this strange device up the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: In Longfellow's poem the banner bears 'a strange device', this Latin word meaning higher still, carried up an Alpine pass.

clue.text: One team takes on a fiery revolutionary

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
an XI, eleven players, is a cricket or football team
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single player joins a side containing a hot-headed rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a rebel, but in Greek myth Ixion was bound to a flaming wheel that turns forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus punished this king by binding him to a burning wheel spinning endlessly, so he revolves amid fire.

clue.text: The family's progressive pedestrian ?

parts.note: split in two, the answer says someone walks forward, '...', while whole it names a son by remarriage within a family

explanation.walkthrough: Read as STEPS ON, the answer is a walker moving forward; read whole, it is a son acquired by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife's or husband's son from an earlier marriage joins the household as a member of the family.

clue.text: She brings news of a possible has-been

indicators.note: a possible arrangement of the letters, one way they could be ordered, signals they are mixed up

explanation.surface: A gossip announces that some faded celebrity may be making news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges the letters of HAS-BEEN. In Irish folklore this female spirit wails to bring news of a coming death.
explanation.definitionFit: The wailing spirit of Irish legend is a herald whose cry foretells a death in the family.
